query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of W with V in equiatomic BCC NbMoTaW (e.g., Nb25Mo25Ta25W15V10 at%) will increase room-temperature tensile ductility and helium-irradiation tolerance without sacrificing single-phase BCC stability or high-temperature (≥1200–1600 °C) mechanical performance. Specifically, the alloy will retain a single BCC solid solution, show 2–5% RT tensile elongation (vs. near-zero for NbMoTaW), maintain high-temperature strength within ~10–15% of baseline, and exhibit reduced helium bubble density/size and delayed blistering onset relative to NbMoTaW under comparable implantation conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or homogenized equiatomic NbMoTaW single-phase BCC alloy with coarse grains (~50–200 µm), known to have excellent strength retention up to ~1600 °C but poor RT tensile ductility and with irradiation tolerance not yet established experimentally.
generation.intervention: Compositional tuning: replace 10 at% of W with V to form Nb25Mo25Ta25W15V10 (at%) and homogenize (e.g., 1250–1350 °C, 24–72 h) followed by rapid quench to retain single-phase BCC and any beneficial short-range order; no other elements added.
generation.conditions: Processing: arc-melt or induction-melt under high-purity Ar, vacuum homogenize at 1250–1350 °C, water quench; optional light warm work and recrystallization to achieve ~20–50 µm grains. Evaluation temperatures: RT to 600 °C for tensile ductility; 1200–1600 °C for compression/creep strength. Irradiation: He implantation at 10–100 keV to 0.5–2×10^22 m^-2 at 300–800 °C; and heavy-ion (e.g., 2 MeV W or Kr) to 5–10 dpa at RT–600 °C for phase stability checks.
generation.structural_mediator: Lower average valence electron concentration and reduced Peierls barrier from V substitution, with preserved BCC single-phase field and high configurational entropy; modest lattice softening and altered short-range order that promotes more mobile dislocations at RT; increased defect recombination and distributed solute/strain fields that raise defect sink strength and suppress He bubble coarsening.
generation.mechanism: V (a ductile BCC refractory with lower shear modulus and lower Peierls stress than W/Mo) reduces lattice friction for screw dislocations, lowering the DBTT and enabling measurable RT tensile ductility. The strong solid-solution field of Nb–Mo–Ta–W is preserved at 10 at% V, maintaining BCC stability and high-temperature strength via solid-solution strengthening and sluggish diffusion at service temperatures. Under irradiation, chemical complexity and lattice distortion enhance recombination of point defects and reduce vacancy supersaturation, decreasing He bubble nucleation/coarsening and delaying blistering. The absence of oversized solutes (e.g., Zr/Hf) minimizes irradiation-enhanced precipitation risks that could destabilize the BCC matrix.
generation.predicted_outcome:
- Phase: single-phase BCC retained after homogenization and after irradiation up to ~10 dpa at ≤600 °C; no amorphization or irradiation-induced intermetallic precipitation detectable by XRD/TEM.
- Room-temperature tensile: uniform + total elongation increases from <1% (baseline) to 2–5%; 0.2% yield strength changes by ≤10–20% relative to baseline (direction uncertain, likely slight decrease at RT).
- High-temperature strength: at 1200–1600 °C, compressive 0.2% offset strength and/or minimum creep rate remain within ~10–15% of equiatomic NbMoTaW under identical test conditions.
- Helium implantation tolerance (10–100 keV, 300–800 °C): near-surface He bubble number density decreases by ~30–50% and mean bubble diameter decreases by ~20–40% at a given fluence; fluence for onset of blistering increases by a factor of ~1.5–2 compared to NbMoTaW. Surface swelling and roughening are reduced accordingly.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic NbMoTaW (single-phase BCC): near-zero RT tensile ductility, excellent high-temperature mechanical strength up to ~1600 °C; irradiation tolerance not established here but serves as the comparison for phase stability, He bubble/blistering behavior, and mechanical property retention.
generation.boundary:
- Composition: V content between ~5 and 20 at% substitution for W; above ~20–25 at% V, risks of excessive softening or altered phase stability may negate high-T performance targets.
- Microstructure: grain sizes ~10–100 µm; ultrafine grains may reduce high-T creep resistance, while extremely coarse grains may not optimize RT ductility.
- Irradiation: predictions apply to He implantation energies ~10–100 keV (near-surface) and heavy-ion doses up to ~10 dpa at ≤600 °C; substantially higher doses/temperatures may enable radiation-enhanced segregation/precipitation not considered here.
- Environment: oxygen pickup should be minimized; significant interstitial contamination (O, N) could embrittle BCC and confound ductility gains.
generation.uncertainty:
- Exact magnitude of RT ductility improvement depends on grain size, texture, and residual impurities; 2–5% is an estimate.
- Direction/magnitude of RT yield strength change could be alloy- and processing-dependent (slight decrease is expected but not certain).
- The degree of bubble density/size reduction and blistering delay under He implantation is estimated; actual gains may vary with energy, fluence, and temperature.
- Extent and role of short-range order in mediating dislocation motion and defect recombination are hypothesized and need direct measurement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare NbMoTaW and Nb25Mo25Ta25W15V10 via identical melting and homogenization; set matched grain sizes (~20–50 µm). Verify single-phase BCC by XRD and APT/TEM. Conduct: (1) RT tensile tests on dogbones to fracture; (2) high-temperature compression or creep at 1200, 1400, and 1600 °C; (3) He implantation at 30 keV to 1×10^22 m^-2 at 300 and 600 °C, then cross-sectional TEM and AFM to assess bubble statistics and blistering; (4) heavy-ion irradiation (2 MeV W or Kr) to 5–10 dpa at 600 °C followed by XRD/TEM/APT to detect amorphization or irradiation-induced precipitation/ordering.
measurements: Phase/microstructure: XRD (phase), EBSD (grain size), TEM/SAED, APT (chemical homogeneity/SRO)
Room-temperature tensile: 0.2% yield strength, UTS, uniform/total elongation
High-temperature performance: 0.2% offset strength in compression and/or minimum creep rate at 1200–1600 °C
He irradiation response: bubble density and size distributions by TEM, cross-sectional swelling, surface blister density/size and onset fluence by AFM/SEM
Irradiation stability: post-ion-irradiation XRD/TEM for amorphization or new phases; APT for segregation/precipitation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if any of the following occur under the stated processing/testing conditions: (a) no statistically significant increase in RT total elongation over NbMoTaW (remains ≤1%); (b) high-temperature (1200–1600 °C) strength or creep resistance degrades by >15% relative to NbMoTaW; (c) He bubble density/size and blistering onset fluence are not improved (≤10% change) or worsen relative to NbMoTaW; or (d) irradiation induces amorphization or second-phase precipitation not present in the baseline alloy at ≤10 dpa and ≤600 °C.
